issue_context.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Pod Resize - resize stuck in "InProgress"
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I am trying the the feature gate "InPlacePodVerticalScaling". I tried on multiple environment/versions and the result is always the same. Resize is forever stuck in "InProgress". 

I followed the doc: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/resize-container-resources/

### What did you expect to happen?

Resize field in pod status should go to `complete`

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Follow this doc: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/resize-container-resources/

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

I tested with kubernetes version 1.27 and 1.29 with the same result.
containerd version being v1.6.28.

The 2 requirements being (from my understanding):
kubernetes >=v1.27
containerd >=v1.6.9


### Cloud provider

I tried on GKE and locally with Minikube


### OS version

mac sonoma 14.1.2 (m1)
comments: /sig node
do you have any logs or detail info?

I don't have more info than this unfortunately. There are no logs, it is in `InProgress` state forever.

I tested it with minikube: `minikube start --kubernetes-version=v1.29.2 --feature-gates=InPlacePodVerticalScaling=true
`
when its in ``InProgress`` you can desc the pod I think, but that might lack of info as well..
Yes, i can `desc` the Pod. There are no related info on the resize unfortunately. Did you succeed to recreate the bug ?

Hi,

I think this is a feature request , not a bug. Perhaps what you are asking for is, to add value `complete` in resize field in the Pod's status to indicate completion of successful resize ? As it is today it is expected behaviour, `complete` is not a defined type  

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9043ce05c125091c0cb5519206fd90d311abd8c8/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L3089-L3098

Related info on the resize can be observed through the allocatedResources values, those have been updated to reflect the new desired CPU requests. If allocatedResources.cpu is equal to resources.limits.cpu indicates that node was able to accommodate the increased CPU resource needs.
Ok thanks @esotsal. What is the point of the `resize` field then ?

> Ok thanks @esotsal. What is the point of the `resize` field then ?

It is used internally in code to control the flow, in addition it helps to troubleshoot failures. 

I understand, from end user perspective/automation, the benefit of your proposal i.e. introduction of a PodResizeStatus value to cater when Pod resources resize has been accepted by node and has been actuated.

I verified same thing by spinning up local cluster using k8s `hack/local-up-cluster.sh` and its works as expected and I dont see any Inprogress resize status even after updating the cpu, I followed the same steps  from [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/resize-container-resources/).

I hit a similar issue when I reproduced #124786. In this case, I set a too small value to the memory limit. Then, I hit the following error and the pod resize status got stuck in “InProgress”:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b5bc8025be6179ff49ea2edf654a6b855ae00119/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L743

I guess you also hit one of  failures in this [doPodResizeAction()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b5bc8025be6179ff49ea2edf654a6b855ae00119/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L664). In this case, you could see what happened only in the kubelet log.


In order to make the failures visible to users, more work seems necessary around `PodSyncResult` and `ReasonCache`:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b5bc8025be6179ff49ea2edf654a6b855ae00119/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1977-L1978
Emitting events might be another option.


After hitting a failure here, the pod worker retries to resize the pod periodically at regular resyncing because no error is returned:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b5bc8025be6179ff49ea2edf654a6b855ae00119/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1989
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b5bc8025be6179ff49ea2edf654a6b855ae00119/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1493-L1494
So, the pod gets stuck in `InProgress`. I'm afraid I’m not sure whether this is an intended behavior or we should abort resizing because I haven't dug this feature yet.

/triage accepted
/assign @esotsal
